messages:
sam: Heads-up — seeing repeated GPU provisioning failures in us-west2 during nightly finetune batches. Jobs stuck in PROVISIONING ~6m then evicted.

maria: Yup, triaged to local-ssd io saturation on workers. IOPS jumped to ~600k on /dev/nvme0n1, avgqu-sz and lat spiked.

evam: logs: run `iostat -x 1 3` and `nvme smart-log` — %util ~99.9, avgqu-sz ~45, and dmesg shows write timeouts.

maria: snippet from dmesg:
```
[    2.345678] nvme0: I/O 0 QID 5 timeout, aborting
[    2.345689] nvme0: write timeout, cd: 0x8
[    2.345699] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678
```

natalie: Is this coinciding with the big batch windows or a stray process? Which instance pools are affected?

sam: p4d-like fleet (batch-gpu-48). Batches of ~80 GPUs kicked off at 02:15 UTC. Same nodes run our ephemeral cleaner cron.

ops-bot: incident created: #1767077000 — tag: storage/high-iops-provisioning-failures

maria: hypothesis: concurrent ephemeral cleaner (scrub) overlaps with massive checkpoint writes => write amplification + small random writes. Cleaner starts reclaiming lots of tiny files while model writers stream checkpoints.

evam: timeline: cleaner cron at 02:10, batch start 02:15, provisioning backlog rises 02:16, kernel write errors 02:18.

sam: quick repro locally with `fio`:
```
fio --name=seqwrite --iodepth=64 --numjobs=32 --bs=128k --rw=write --size=10G
```
That reproduces avgq-sz jumps and stalls.

maria: immediate mitigation idea: throttle cleaner concurrency from 12 -> 4 and add a token-bucket rate limiter to its writer. Also back off scrub when nvme avg latency > 10ms.

evam: agreed. Quick kube change: add a precondition to cleaner controller to check `node.nvme.avg_latency < 10ms` before starting reclaim. PR ready: `gitlab.com/redwood/infra/changes/cleanup-throttle`.

sam: canary in eu-west first. Also watch SMART wear counters — we saw `Media_Wear` bump on 3 nodes. Don’t want to accelerate wear by aggressive retries.

maria: cost aside: fallback to on-demand after provisioning failure caused a big spend spike — ~$4k last night due to churn and retries on fallback pools. Need guardrails.

natalie: Ops asks: can we avoid immediate fallback to on-demand if queue time < 5m? That would prevent flip-flopping and double-billing.

evam: simple patch: add `provisioning.fallback.min_queue_seconds = 300` and only trigger fallback after that threshold. I'll open PR after canary.

ops-bot: deploy plan: scrub-throttle-v1 -> canary eu-west2 -> monitor 30m -> roll us-west2.

deploy-bot: scrub-throttle-v1 rolled to eu-west2-canary at 1767077200.

evam: canary looks green: avg nvme latency down ~30%, provisioning success up from 70% -> 92% in the window.

sam: good. roll to us-west2 in 15m. Also create a follow-up ticket to add a hot-spot detector: watch per-node avgqsz and nvme_throughput and evacuate scheduled batches if threshold hit.

maria: filing INF-4523 with notes, timeline, PR links, and suggested owner @maria. I'll add dashboard tiles for `node:local_nvme.avgqsz`, `node:local_nvme.write_amp`, and `cleaner.concurrency`.

natalie: +1. Also add runbook step: if provisioning fails with nvme write errors, temporarily pause cleaner and delay new batch rollouts by 10 minutes.

sam: follow-up: add cost flag to provisioning to disallow fallback to on-demand if queued < 5m to avoid churn. Evan to PR.

maria: thanks everyone — I'll own the postmortem and the dashboard. Will update INF-4523 when scrub-throttle is rolled to us-west2.

ops-bot: incident #1767077000 status -> monitoring; next update in 30m.
